findings.how_to_check: Examine replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do: lines 30-31 contain the only assert statements in the file; lines 57-76 only format and display the values without evaluating relative or absolute differences.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit tolerance checks (e.g., asserting that current linkage and validation rates fall within acceptable percentage bounds of the historical rates) or calculate differences and output a clear PASS/FAIL summary for each row.
findings.title: The reproduction diagnostic never decides whether the Rhode Island results were reproduced
findings.what_the_code_does: The script hardcodes rounded historical August statistics in local macros and displays them side-by-side with current recomputed statistics using formatted display statements. While lines 30-31 assert that exactly one state was matched and observations exist, the script contains no assertions, calculated discrepancies, or tolerance checks comparing the current statistics to the historical benchmarks.
findings.why_it_matters: The script poses the question 'DOES THE CURRENT CODE REPRODUCE THE RHODE ISLAND RESULTS?' in its header, but can exit with code 0 even if current figures deviate substantially from the historical benchmark. It functions as an eyeball comparison rather than an automated, repeatable replication test.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims in the paper draft could not be compared against code directly; claims-vs-code review was limited to the uncommitted diagnostic script and notes.
External census and link datasets reside outside the repository on local/network storage and were not directly loaded or manipulated.
The Stata pipeline was not executed during this review run; all runtime behavior, macro expansion, and summary statistics were evaluated by static source code analysis.
Review scope was restricted to the uncommitted changes in the working tree (replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do and review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md), not a full repository audit.
structured_output.summary: The uncommitted Rhode Island diagnostic correctly filters the state sample and faithfully mirrors the all-state linkage and validation rate definitions from create_figures_SSHA2025.do. Its primary limitation is that it prints the historical August draft values alongside current calculations without defining tolerance bounds or evaluating pass/fail criteria. No data mutation or econometric correctness defects were found in the uncommitted files.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do:25-31 applies `strpos(lower(state_folder_name), "rhode") > 0`, inspects unique values with `levelsof`, and asserts `: word count `st'' == 1 and `_N > 0`.
verified_clean.item: The Rhode Island filter cannot silently select zero or multiple state labels.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do:34 uses `gen target = !(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast)`, which exactly matches CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:117.
verified_clean.item: The diagnostic uses the same target definition as the current all-state table.

verified_clean.evidence: CODE/clean_FS_and_combineV5_nber.do:225 requires `namelast!="" & namefrst!="" & namefrst_fs!="" & namelast_fs!="" & age!=. & age_fs!=.` before creating the labeled dataset read into temp.dta.
verified_clean.item: Blank-name equality cannot inflate the target comparison under the upstream data builder.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do:60-75 uses total count `r(N)` for linkage rates and separate non-missing counts `r(N)` from `summarize validated_before` and `summarize validated_after`, mirroring CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:158-166,203-209.
verified_clean.item: Linkage and validation denominators mirror the current table implementation.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do:16-81 opens a dedicated log file and only executes read-only queries (`use`, `count`, `sum`, `display`) with no `save`, `replace` of datasets, or exports.
verified_clean.item: The new diagnostic does not mutate analysis datasets or workspace state.

verified_clean.evidence: review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md:7-18 explicitly marks tentative numbers for verification and correctly identifies an unsupported training data claim for excision.
verified_clean.item: The revision notes distinguish unverified claims from definite corrections.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/diagnostics/ri_replication.do:25-79 restricts its analysis to descriptive comparison of linkage and validation means.
verified_clean.item: The uncommitted code introduces no causal specification or new link selection mechanism.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
